narr: As Tropical Storm Eta continues to approach the FL coast in the NE Gulf of Mexico, bands of trailing showers and embedded thunderstorms spread across South Florida from the SSW to the NNE. Some of these bands contained heavy rain and gusty winds. With generally SSW steering flow in place, brief periods of training convection occurred. Due to super saturated antecedent conditions, minimal rain contributed to flooding across the east coast of South Florida.
ev: A Miami Herald reporter and members of the public posted videos of significant flooding in the Biscayne Point, Normandy Isles, and North Beach neighborhoods of Miami Beach. Streets were impassable and several cars were stranded. Water also encroached on several homes. ||Rain gauges in the area measured between 3.6 and 4.7 inches of rain in 3 hours between 5:15 PM and 8:15 PM, with daily totals in the 4-6 inch range.

Several reports of flash flooding in Biscayne Park and North Miami were received. Roads were impassable in Biscayne Park with water entering crawlspaces and homes. Streets were also impassable at the intersection of Biscayne Boulevard and Sans Souci Boulevard in North Miami. Rain gauges in the area measured 3-4 inches of rain, most of it over the course of a couple of hours.
